STATE_VECTOR.seeding: top_price = h[0], bottom_price = l[0] — seeded from the FIRST BAR (the 2026-08-15 fix), not from zero
STATE_VECTOR.separation: OUTPUT_t = f(STATE_{t-1}, OBS_t) and STATE_t = g(STATE_{t-1}, OBS_t) analysed separately, to avoid the off-by-one trap that the g* latch exposed

COLLAPSE_ANALYSIS.question: does any observed event force all admissible prior states to the same next state?
COLLAPSE_ANALYSIS.finding: NO unconditional overwrite exists anywhere in the loop. Every state update is guarded by a condition that itself depends on prior state.
COLLAPSE_ANALYSIS.critical_variables: top_price and bottom_price are MONOTONE RUNNING EXTREMES: "if l[i] < bottom_price: bottom_price = l[i]". This is precisely the non-collapsing form — old state survives unless exceeded, and no finite observation can overwrite it for all admissible priors.
COLLAPSE_ANALYSIS.contrast_with_WLNBB: WLNBB ffill carriers ARE re-anchored, because ffill_when OVERWRITES the level at each qualifying bar. A running extreme never overwrites; it only narrows. That is why the same reasoning yields opposite answers for the two engines.
COLLAPSE_ANALYSIS.contrast_with_g_star: the g* latch collapses because g_armed := (g_armed OR trigger) AND NOT any_g forces False on any firing bar. CISD has no analogous forcing branch.

fixture_1.design: two real prefixes (bars 0..1499 vs 800..1499) then 700 identical post-gap bars
fixture_1.interpretation: NOT evidence of collapse — the fixture failed to separate the states, because the post-gap window contained new extremes that overwrote both priors. Recorded as an inconclusive test, not as a pass.

fixture_2.design: synthetic priors chosen so post-gap lows fall BETWEEN their extremes (prefix A low ~86.6, prefix B low ~98.1, post-gap low min 99.1) — so the l[i] < bottom_price branch fires for one prior and not the other

CISD_PPM.note: not separated by this fixture — both zero. Inherits non-identifiability from the plus/minus stream it consumes.

fixture_2.interpretation: identical post-gap observations, different admissible priors, materially different outputs — up to a 3.4x difference in fire count

CONSEQUENCE.rule: after an interior UNOBSERVED_CONTAMINATED gap, all four CISD outputs remain INITIALIZATION_SENSITIVE_POST_GAP until the end of the segment
CONSEQUENCE.no_softening: this is NOT relaxed to preserve support. No default-state reset is permitted, because source equivalence for such a reset was not shown — it was disproved.
CONSEQUENCE.series_head: SERIES HEAD is different: no prior Massive history exists at all, so the canonical seed (top_price=h[0], bottom_price=l[0]) defines a NEW MASSIVE measurement regime rather than an unknown-state problem. Classified INITIALIZATION_SENSITIVE_HEAD and distinguished from the post-gap case.

EXPECTED_SUPPORT_IMPACT.note: Stage A measured COMPLETE-run median length of 2 bars on a pilot security. If post-gap state is never recoverable, CISD valid support is bounded by the FIRST contiguous COMPLETE run of each security only.
EXPECTED_SUPPORT_IMPACT.status: NOT YET MEASURED — this is the quantity C4/C5 must establish before any CISD column can be considered for the search surface

OUTPUT_DEPENDENCY_SETS: not separately established — all four consume plus_arr/minus_arr, which depend on the non-identifiable structure state, so the family shares the blocking condition
